description: Author a new primitive of this repository's charter, asking cw what its kind requires.
Answer what the sessions kept on this machine cost, per session and per day, at prices the developer types in or the model provider publishes.
Count the session's tokens when the agent stops, keep them on this machine, and say so at every mark.
Count the session's tokens each time the agent stops.
Check the spec set for gaps, contradictions and format faults, and report each by id with its fix; changes nothing.

Fix one bug on a fix branch of its own — understand it, reproduce it with evidence, report the root cause and the fix for approval, fix it test first, review, verify, and finish into the development branch.
What every change to code walked by a playbook of the spec set is held to: the manifest first, and a change handed over only once checked.
List the story and phase branches whose work has already landed, and delete the ones the user confirms, with their worktrees.
Why specs are split by part with a status per story, why a roadmap sits beside them, why they hold no how, and why every phase stops at a gate.
Finish the story, bug fix or phase you stand on exactly as manifest.md says — merge, squash-merge or pull request, into the branch it names — then clean its worktree up.
Implement a ready story of the spec set — pick it, spec gate, test first, verify, review — the way manifest.md says, and mark it Done.

Set a repository up for spec-driven development — find the specs it already has and offer to refactor them into a spec set, ask how work is carried out and finished, then write .sdd/settings.json, the spec folder and its manifest.md.
The iron laws every change to code walked by a playbook of the spec set is held to, closing the playbook: evidence before a claim, no commit the manifest does not allow.
Write what this conversation taught — a correction, a preference, a constraint — as a note in learning/inbox.
Never save to the agent's own memory; write what was learned into learning/inbox, where repeated lessons become rules.
Find where the code a story or a bug runs through lives, and name it as path:line ranges with a reason each; reads only, changes nothing.
The skeleton of manifest.md — how work is carried out and finished in a repository, as /sdd-init asked the user.
Write a phase's stories, FR and SC into the right spec-<key>.md and plan.json, clarifying what is unclear first; no plan of how, no task list.
Draw the roadmap — every story of plan.json, where it stands and what it waits on — into report.html in the spec folder, and say what it shows.
Review the change against the story's scenarios, FR and SC — nothing missing, nothing beyond them — and for security issues.
The skeleton of one spec-<key>.md, its ids under the prefix its key makes — copied when a spec set gains a part.
The shape of a spec set — spec.md as index, spec-<key>.md with prefixed ids, plan.json, manifest.md, ADR.md — what and why, never how.
The skeleton of spec.md, the index of a spec set — copied by /sdd-init.
Link every id the specs cite, check the specs against plan.json, and list the stories that can start now.
Link every id the specs cite and check them against plan.json, and refuse to stop while either fails.
List every story of the spec set with its status, and the stories that can be built now.
Prove the change works with evidence produced this turn — tests, static checks, and a manual run of what the story describes.
How a playbook of the spec set talks to the user: the answer first, a line per step, every name and error verbatim, in full sentences of the user's language.
Why lessons go to learning/inbox rather than an agent's memory, and how a note there is written.
